answer: Each identity charters one voyage and locks an 80-credit bond. The atlas publishes voyage distance, pigment cargo weight, copper calibration, and charter invoice; any auditor recomputes the charge from the public rate table, checks the zenith ceiling, and burns the bond on a short, reused, or over-ceiling invoice. The k-th voyage pays 90+18(k-1) credits, so 1,000 fakes pay 9,081,000 in fees plus 80,000 locked. A rented-charter ring fails: the atlas rejects a duplicate invoice hash, and one voyage cannot cover two charters. An honest charterer pays 90 once, bond back after a clean epoch.
